astronaut.q: How many fingers on one hand?
astronaut.fact: Most people have five fingers on each hand, including the thumb.

astronaut.q: How many days in a week?
astronaut.fact: A week has seven days, from Monday through Sunday.

astronaut.q: How many legs does a spider have?
astronaut.fact: Spiders are arachnids, and adult spiders have eight legs.

astronaut.q: How many wheels on a car?
astronaut.fact: Most everyday cars have four wheels touching the road.

astronaut.q: How many months in a year?
astronaut.fact: A year is divided into twelve months.

astronaut.q: How many eyes do you have?
astronaut.fact: People usually have two eyes that work together to help us see.

astronaut.q: Which shape has 3 sides?
astronaut.fact: A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.

astronaut.q: Which shape is round?
astronaut.fact: A circle is round and has no straight sides or corners.

astronaut.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides?
astronaut.fact: A square has four equal sides and four right-angle corners.

astronaut.q: A football is shaped like a...
astronaut.fact: A sphere is round in every direction, like a ball.

astronaut.q: What shape is a dice?
astronaut.fact: A standard die is a cube with six square faces.

astronaut.q: Which shape has 5 points?
astronaut.fact: A five-pointed star has five points around its outline.

astronaut.q: What organ pumps blood around your body?
astronaut.fact: The heart is a strong muscle that pumps blood around the body.

astronaut.q: What do you use to breathe?
astronaut.fact: Your lungs take oxygen from the air when you breathe in.

astronaut.q: What do you think with?
astronaut.fact: The brain helps you think, remember, feel and control your body.

astronaut.q: What covers your whole body?
astronaut.fact: Skin protects your body and helps you feel touch, heat and cold.

astronaut.q: What helps you chew food?
astronaut.fact: Teeth bite and chew food into smaller pieces.

astronaut.q: What do you use to hear sounds?
astronaut.fact: Your ears collect sound and send signals to your brain.

astronaut.q: Which animal is the King of the Jungle?
astronaut.fact: The lion is sometimes called “king of the jungle”, but lions usually live in grasslands.

astronaut.q: Which animal has a long trunk?
astronaut.fact: An elephant uses its trunk to smell, breathe, drink and pick things up.

astronaut.q: Which animal says "Moo"?
astronaut.fact: Cows are grown-up female cattle; their familiar call is a moo.

astronaut.q: Which animal can fly?
astronaut.fact: Eagles are birds. Their large wings help them soar on air currents.

astronaut.q: Which is the tallest animal?
astronaut.fact: A giraffe’s long neck helps it reach leaves high in trees.

astronaut.q: Which animal lives in the sea?
astronaut.fact: Dolphins are mammals that breathe air at the surface and live in water.

astronaut.q: Which animal is the fastest on land?
astronaut.fact: Cheetahs can sprint faster than other land animals over short distances.

astronaut.q: Which dinosaur had tiny arms?
astronaut.fact: Tyrannosaurus rex had two very small arms and two powerful legs.

astronaut.q: Which dinosaur had 3 horns?
astronaut.fact: Triceratops had three horns on its head and a large bony frill.

astronaut.q: Which dinosaur had plates on its back?
astronaut.fact: Stegosaurus had rows of large plates along its back.

astronaut.q: Which prehistoric reptile could fly?
astronaut.fact: Pterosaurs were flying reptiles; they were not dinosaurs.

astronaut.q: What did dinosaurs hatch from?
astronaut.fact: Dinosaurs hatched from eggs, just as many animals do today.

astronaut.q: Are non-bird dinosaurs still alive today?
astronaut.fact: Non-bird dinosaurs are extinct, but modern birds are living dinosaur relatives.

astronaut.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
astronaut.fact: The Sun is a star. It looks bigger and brighter because it is much closer than other stars.

astronaut.q: How many planets in our solar system?
astronaut.fact: There are eight planets orbiting the Sun in our solar system.

astronaut.q: What planet are we on?
astronaut.fact: Earth is the planet where people, animals and plants live.

astronaut.q: Which planet has beautiful rings?
astronaut.fact: Saturn’s rings are made mostly of pieces of ice and rock.

astronaut.q: What do astronauts wear in space?
astronaut.fact: A spacesuit supplies air and helps protect an astronaut in space.

astronaut.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
astronaut.fact: Mars looks rusty red because iron-rich dust covers much of its surface.

astronaut.q: What pulls things down to the ground?
astronaut.fact: Gravity is a force that pulls objects toward Earth.

astronaut.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
astronaut.fact: He was the very first person to walk on the Moon!

astronaut.q: Who was the first person ever to go to space?
astronaut.fact: He was the first person ever to fly to space!

astronaut.q: Who went to the Moon with Neil Armstrong?
astronaut.fact: He went to the Moon with Neil and took a selfie in space!

astronaut.q: Who was the first Black woman to travel to space?
astronaut.fact: She was the first Black woman to travel to space!

astronaut.q: Who was the first American woman in space?
astronaut.fact: She was the first American woman to go to space!

astronaut.q: Which astronaut sang a song from space?
astronaut.fact: He played guitar and sang a song while floating in space!

astronaut.q: What was the name of the first dog sent to orbit Earth?
astronaut.fact: She was the first dog to orbit Earth in a spacecraft.

astronaut.q: Which British astronaut ran a marathon in space?
astronaut.fact: He ran a race on a treadmill while flying through space!
